description: Somos Inteligencia Artesanal, un equipo que combina creatividad humana e inteligencia artificial para desarrollar software y aplicaciones a medida. Nos apasiona transformar ideas en soluciones útiles, competir en hackathones y aprender con cada reto.
summary: LUUMIA is a decision-support tool that helps smallholder farmers see what each crop rotation could leave them, not just what it could yield. Farmers like Don Tino, in Yucatán, Mexico, already plan their planting and care for their soil, yet after subtracting costs they often keep less than expected. LUUMIA combines a field’s history (past seasons, yields and soil) with NASA Earth observation data (NASA POWER climate, GPM IMERG rainfall, SMAP soil moisture and MODIS/VIIRS vegetation indices) and export reference prices to compare rotation scenarios side by side, showing expected yield, costs and estimated margin per hectare for each one. This addresses the Field Shift challenge by connecting soil health and climate adaptation with the farmer’s own priority: income. It matters because a rotation that is good for the soil will only be adopted if it is also viable for the family that farms it. What you sow matters. So does what you keep.
details:
LuumIA is a crop planning tool for farmers and cooperatives in southeastern Mexico. It helps answer three questions before planting: What should I grow? How much land should I dedicate to each crop? What could I earn from the harvest?

Farmers enter their field size, crop history, and field observations. LuumIA uses the latest recorded crop cycle to compare rotation options based on crop-family diversity. Farmers can then drag the boundaries on a field sketch to adjust how many hectares go to each crop. The simulator estimates harvest and profit using expected yields, crop losses, prices, costs, and how much buyers can purchase. Cooperatives can review shared plans and compare projected profit with recorded sales.

We built the web app with React, TypeScript, and Vite, and the backend with Python, FastAPI, and PostgreSQL. We used NASA POWER for regional weather, HLS for vegetation imagery, and SMAP and IMERG for regional soil moisture and rainfall maps. We also used Mexican agricultural and market data from DGSIAP and SNIIM, alongside USDA references. We tested field capture with KoboCollect on Android using a simulated rain-gauge reading.

LuumIA’s creative contribution is connecting crop rotation advice to a plan farmers can adjust before committing land and money. We designed the farmer view for quick decisions on a phone, with technical details available one level deeper. We also considered the scale and age of satellite data, missing field measurements, and uncertainty in prices and yields. The app labels observations, forecasts, and assumptions so users can judge what applies to their field.

Our intended impact is to help farmers diversify crops while managing income risk, and to give cooperatives a clearer view of expected harvests before they arrange purchases. The demo follows Don Tino, a fictional farmer in Campeche, as he divides 10 hectares between squash and beans and shares his plan for review.
